newsitem.title: USA: Employee Solutions sees weak results, stock falls further.
newsitem.headline: Employee Solutions sees weak results, stock falls further.

text.p: Employee Solutions Inc., a provider of temporary workers, Friday confirmed that it expects disappointing fourth-quarter earnings, fuelling an extended sell-off of its stock in heavy trading.
The stock had already lost half its value on Thursday after the company said it was delaying indefinitely the release of its fourth-quarter results.
Employee Solutions fell $9.125, or nearly 60 percent, to $6.25 on Nasdaq, where it was the most active issue at mid-morning.
On Thursday the stock fell $4.50 to $15.375 during normal trading hours, and dropped further to $10 after the company made the announcement about the delay.

The stock was further punished by rumours that its chairman and chief executive, Marvin Brody, has been selling unregistered shares of the company in Europe, which caused panic-selling among investors. Brody denied the rumours.
Employee Solutions said its fourth-quarter results will be below analysts' estimates, but noted that it will report a profit for both the quarter and full year.
The Phoenix, Ariz.-based company provided no specific figures, and company officials were not available for comment.
Employee Solutions said it intends to report its results for the year and fourth quarter "as soon as practicable" but is unable at this time to estimate when that will be.
